image.prompt:
Straight-on ELEVATION photograph of one whole high-rise building, taken from very far away with a long telephoto lens: the camera is level with the building's mid-height, so every vertical edge is perfectly vertical and parallel with no keystone convergence, and the main facade is seen frontally with only a thin sliver of one side. Not a three-quarter view, not an aerial view, not looking up from the street.

The building: Very long thirty-storey affordable residential slab block, plain cream painted concrete with a dense repeating grid of small square windows and tiny balconies with steel grilles, three vertical stairwell strips of open louvres painted the same pale cream as the facade dividing the facade into bays, a flat roof with a row of water tanks and a blue painted band at the parapet Materials: cream painted render heavily rain-streaked grey, blue paint band at the parapet, pale cream painted concrete louvre strips with grey streaking, rusty steel window grilles.

Whole building: the complete tower from its ground-floor base to the very top of its crown, roof plant, spire or antenna, with nothing cropped. The base sits at the bottom of the silhouette with nothing in front of it: no trees, no street, no cars, no people, no neighbouring buildings, no scaffolding. The only text is lettering explicitly described above; otherwise no signs, no logos, no watermarks, no annotations.

Framing: the building is centred and fills about 85% of the frame along its longer axis, with a clear empty margin on every side.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080) fills every part of the frame that is not the building, including where the sky would be and where the ground would be. The building is a cut-out floating against an infinite flat backdrop. No sky, no clouds, no horizon, no ground plane, no cast shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient, no haze, no atmospheric fade.

Lighting: bright overcast daylight, flat and even, soft and shadowless, so the facade reads as true albedo with its glass tint, concrete and paint colours exactly as described. No sun glare, no specular blowout, no lens flare, no dramatic sky colour reflected in the glass.

One building only. Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, every floor, window, mullion and balcony resolved, realistic weathering and grime. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render, not a wireframe, not low-poly.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Long Slab Residential Tower

notes: Wider than tall, so the plate is 4:3 and the width is the framed axis. This is the backdrop filler of the batch: dense and repetitive so multiple copies stack up as a housing estate on the horizon. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 4:3, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand. Plate retune 2026-08-27: the louvre strips were described as grey concrete, which rendered at the backdrop's own #808080 and cut the facade into separate components for prepare-image.mjs on two seeds (101, 102); repainted cream in prompts.image and prompts.texture so the silhouette keys as one piece. Plate note 2026-08-27: with the louvre strips repainted the seed-103 plate is one component but framed at 73% coverage, with the ground-floor windows inside the bottom-5% contact-shadow band (17%); rows below the base measure a flat 140 apart from a one-row plinth edge line. Extended 10% top and bottom with the measured backdrop (140) before the gate, which passed it; imposter.png is the padded raw.
